show-clusters-help: Access Score is built on these footpath label clusters. Clusters appear once you zoom in to street level. You can click on clusters to see their underlying imagery.
chart-histogram-help: How much footpath sits at each score. Drag across the bars to pick a range; the map dims everything outside it.
show-grade-help: Colors every street by how steep it is instead of by its AccessScore. Gradient comes from an elevation model, not from labels, so unaudited streets have it too. While this is on, every street with a gradient is drawn, so “Show unaudited streets” has no effect.
slope-quality-structure: This street is on a bridge or in a tunnel, which the elevation model cannot see, so it has no gradient.
slope-quality-suspect: The elevation model looked unreliable here, so this gradient is a straight line between the street's two ends.
profile-legend-title: Length at each gradient, per {{spacing}} stretch
slope-help: How much a steep street lowers its score. Between the two thresholds the penalty grows from nothing to the full weight; set the weight to 0 to leave gradient out of the score. Only streets that already have a score are affected. Gradient is measured along each street's centerline; cross slope, the tilt across a footpath, is not measured.
slope-barrier-help: A segment whose steepest stretch is over this gradient scores 0, whatever its footpaths are like. The street's score still averages in the crossings at its ends.
slope-approximate-include-help: Some gradients are only a straight line between a street's two ends: where a city has only a coarse elevation model, or where the model looked unreliable. Turn this on to let those gradients count too.
